chris: Quick microbench run — L4 vs T4 vs A10G on embeddings + small-chat across us-east-1 / eu-west-1. Posting config & raw numbers. Looking for kernel/packing recs and whether int8 affected quality. benchbot: starting run... 
benchbot: Command used:
```
./run_microbench --model l4/t4/a10g --mode {emb,chat} --quant {fp16,int8} --region {us-east-1,eu-west-1} --batch 8 --seq 128
```
benchbot: Results CSV snippet:
```
model,region,mode,quant,p50_ms,p95_ms,qps,tokens_s,cost_1M_tokens_usd
L4,us-east-1,emb,int8,12,28,850,34000,14.2
T4,us-east-1,emb,int8,15,40,720,29000,9.8
A10G,us-east-1,emb,fp16,9,20,1300,52000,22.5
L4,eu-west-1,chat,int8,38,95,120,6000,18.0
T4,eu-west-1,chat,int8,45,120,95,4800,12.5
A10G,eu-west-1,chat,fp16,25,60,210,10500,26.4
```
anya: Nice. Did you pin kernel choices or let the runtime pick? any special compilation flags? :eyes:
benchbot: Runtime used auto-kernel selection; we forced `--kernel-policy performance` for A10G and `--kernel-policy cost` for T4 runs. No custom kernels.
kevin: Node packing notes — T4 runs used 2 gpus/node, L4 were 8-gpu shards, A10G single-gpu with big memory. Batching behavior was continuous-batch with max_batch=16.
rachel: Quality check — we ran 1k eval prompts for embeddings and 500 small-chat evals. Summary: int8 embeddings cos-sim delta ~ -0.007 mean; small-chat acceptability drop ~1.5% on human-sim score (mostly minor hallucinations increase).
chris: TL;DR: For embeddings cost-sensitive workloads T4 int8 wins on cost per 1M tokens but higher p95; A10G best latency and throughput for low-latency chat. L4 is middle ground but good when you need predictable latency at moderate cost.
anya: Any kernel recommendations? maybe xvli kernel for A10G? also are we doing KV cache shards differently per gpu?
kevin: For chat keep `kernel: fused-attn` + `kv-shard=per-device` on A10G. For T4 try `kernel: tiling` + `quant=dynamic-int8`. L4 we saw best with `kernel: attention32`.
rachel: We should flag the int8 quality delta in the eval dashboard and add a regression alert if embedding cosine drops >0.01. I'll file a quick ticket.
chris: Good. Next steps: run a scaled sweep (3-hour) with canary routing enabled, validate canary against eval-set, then propose dedicated-capacity packing policy. Anyone want to take the sweep?
anya: I'll kick off the sweep later today and post logs. :+1:
kevin: I'll prepare packing config and 2-node T4 template.
rachel: Filing ticket now — ENGML-4321. :memo:
benchbot: sweep scheduled: 2619880200. I'll post final aggregated CSV there. :robot_face:
chris: Thanks all, useful quick turn. :fire:
